source: Original (authored October 2026, calculator allowed). Cosine rule on three triangles: (a) sides 8 and 11 with included angle 40 deg, find x; (b)(c) sides 5, 7, 9, largest angle theta and classification; (d) sides 6 and 10 with included angle 120 deg, exact y.

parts.label: a
parts.description: Triangle with sides 8 and 11 and included angle 40 deg; x is the side opposite the 40 deg angle. Find x.
parts.tolerance: Accept 7.08 or the display with an ellipsis (7.08351...). A value cut short without an ellipsis (7.1, 7.084) earns A0. A radian-mode value (17.4) earns M1A0.
parts.notes: M1 for a correct substitution into the cosine rule: x^2 = 8^2 + 11^2 - 2(8)(11)cos 40. A1 for 7.08.

parts.label: b
parts.description: Triangle with sides 5, 7, 9. Find the largest angle theta (opposite the side 9).
parts.tolerance: Accept 95.7 or the display with an ellipsis (95.7391...). A value cut short without an ellipsis (95.74, 96) earns A0.
parts.notes: M1 for a correct substitution into the cosine rule with 9^2 as the subtracted term: cos theta = (5^2 + 7^2 - 9^2)/(2(5)(7)), or 9^2 = 5^2 + 7^2 - 2(5)(7)cos theta. A1 for 95.7. An angle found opposite the side 5 or 7 earns M0A0.

parts.label: c
parts.description: State whether the triangle with sides 5, 7, 9 is acute, right-angled or obtuse.
parts.tolerance: Accept 'obtuse' with or without a reason (theta > 90, or cos theta < 0, or 9^2 > 5^2 + 7^2).
parts.follow_through: FT from the candidate's angle in (b): 'acute' earns A1 if their largest angle is below 90 degrees.

parts.label: d
parts.description: Triangle with sides 6 and 10 and included angle 120 deg; y is the side opposite the 120 deg angle. Find the exact value of y.
parts.tolerance: Accept 14 or sqrt(196). A decimal such as 14.0 earns A1.
parts.notes: M1 for a correct substitution into the cosine rule: y^2 = 6^2 + 10^2 - 2(6)(10)cos 120. A1 for 14. The sign slip y^2 = 136 - 60 = 76, y = 8.72 earns M1A0.

source: Original (authored October 2026, calculator allowed). Hikers 6 km and 9 km along paths at 35 deg; quadrilateral ABCD with AB = 5, BC = 8, CD = 6, AD = 4, angle ABC = 60 deg.

parts.label: a
parts.description: Two hikers leave a campsite along straight paths with 35 deg between them. One walks 6 km, the other 9 km. Find the distance between them.
parts.tolerance: Accept 5.34 or the display with an ellipsis (5.34149...). Units not required. A value cut short without an ellipsis (5.3, 5.341) earns A0.
parts.notes: M1 for a correct substitution into the cosine rule: d^2 = 6^2 + 9^2 - 2(6)(9)cos 35. A1 for 5.34. A diagram is not required.

parts.label: b
parts.description: In quadrilateral ABCD, AB = 5 cm, BC = 8 cm, angle ABC = 60 deg. Find the diagonal AC.
parts.notes: M1 for a correct substitution into the cosine rule: AC^2 = 5^2 + 8^2 - 2(5)(8)cos 60. A1 for 7.

parts.label: c
parts.description: In quadrilateral ABCD, CD = 6 cm, AD = 4 cm. Using AC from (b), find angle ADC.
parts.tolerance: Accept 86.4 or the display with an ellipsis (86.4166...). A value cut short without an ellipsis (86.42, 86) earns A0.
parts.notes: M1 for a correct substitution into the cosine rule in triangle ACD with AC^2 as the subtracted term: cos ADC = (4^2 + 6^2 - AC^2)/(2(4)(6)). A1 for 86.4.
parts.follow_through: FT from the candidate's AC in (b).
